sop_title: NETCINST 4200.4A - Government-Wide Commercial Purchase Card (GCPC) Program Internal Operating Procedures
summary: The procedure covers the purchase card cycle at NETC: appointing and training cardholders, obtaining funding and approvals, making and receiving micro-purchases, monthly reconciliation and certification, and handling disputes and fraud. It is run by Cardholders (CHs), the Approving/Certifying Official (AO/CO), N8 (funding), N4 (GCPC Program Manager acting as A/OPC and AO), and the A/OPC with CITIBANK.

steps.action: Nominates the employee to become a cardholder; the A/OPC is notified of the new participant.
steps.source_quote: The CH will be nominated by the requesting department by email or memo.

steps.action: Completes required initial training and provides copies of all training certificates to the A/OPC.
steps.source_quote: Prior to making purchases, the CH will complete initial training

steps.action: Appoints the CH by delegation of authority. The delegation specifies spending limits and authorized transaction types. SF 1402 is used if the CH's authority exceeds the micro-purchase threshold.
steps.source_quote: The CH will be appointed using SF 1402 (Certificate of Appointment) if their procurement authority exceeds the micro-purchase threshold.

steps.action: Acknowledges responsibility and understanding of reference (a) and this instruction.
steps.source_quote: The CH will acknowledge the responsibility and understanding of reference (a)

steps.action: Emails the centrally managed purchase requirement to N8.
steps.input: Requirement for supplies, services, or training
steps.source_quote: Requests are emailed to N8.

steps.action: Reviews unusual or questionable requests before any action is taken.
steps.input: Unusual or questionable request forwarded by N8
steps.source_quote: Unusual or questionable requests are forwarded to the Deputy Comptroller, Comptroller, and possibly Legal (N00D) for review prior to taking action.

steps.action: Assigns the appropriate LOA and document number to the routine request. Sends both to the requestor and to the CH with a request to make the purchase.
steps.output: LOA and document number; purchase request to CH
steps.source_quote: If funding is available, routine requests are processed by assigning the appropriate LOA.

steps.action: Reviews requirements for which funding is exhausted.
steps.source_quote: If funding is exhausted, requirements are forwarded to the Comptroller for review.

steps.action: Completes the required additional documentation (SF 182 or NETC 4235/4), obtains approval signatures, and provides signed copies to N8 and the CH.
steps.source_quote: the requestor completes the required documentation, obtains the appropriate signatures for approval

steps.action: Prepares the SF 182 with an LOA, the GCPC payment statement, and the CH's name and phone number (obtained from N4). Provides a copy to N4 before forwarding to the Human Resources Office.
steps.output: SF 182 copy to N4; SF 182 to HRO
steps.source_quote: Provide a copy of SF 182 to N4 prior to forwarding to Human Resources Office.

steps.action: Screens the purchase request against mandatory supply sources such as Ability One. Procures office supplies from DoD EMALL or SERVMART using NETC 4400/1, and printing from DLA Document Services.
steps.source_quote: Screen the purchase request from mandatory supply sources (i.e., Ability One)

steps.action: Approves the purchase before the CH buys.
steps.source_quote: Obtain AO approval prior to purchasing.

steps.action: Approves a purchase that exceeds the CH's single purchase limit.
steps.source_quote: The single purchase limit cannot be exceeded unless approved by N4.

steps.action: Confirms the merchant agrees to the order terms: no charge until shipment, no back orders, delivery within 30 days, and required shipping document information.
steps.source_quote: The CH must confirm that the merchant agrees

steps.action: Places the order over the counter, by phone, or via the internet. Reminds the merchant not to charge sales tax and seeks FOB destination terms.
steps.input: Fair and reasonable price; merchant agreement
steps.source_quote: If the merchant's price is fair and reasonable, CH may proceed to purchase the supplies.

steps.action: Records the transaction and supporting documentation in the purchase card log.
steps.source_quote: A purchase card log, NETC 4430/1, is required to record all purchase card transactions.

steps.action: Receives and inspects the supplies or services, with legible signature and date.
steps.source_quote: one will perform receipt/inspection

steps.action: Accepts the supplies or services, with legible signature and date.
steps.source_quote: one will accept. These actions must be accomplished by legible signature and date.

steps.action: Determine whether the material must be recorded in a formal property management or accounting system.
steps.source_quote: AOs and CHs identify whether materials need to be recorded in a formal property management or accounting system.

steps.action: Records accountable property in DPAS.
steps.source_quote: All materials classified as accountable property will be recorded in the Defense Property Accounting System (DPAS).

steps.action: At the end of the billing cycle, verifies each transaction on the statement. Ensures every purchase is documented on the log and charged or reallocated to the proper LOA.
steps.source_quote: The CH will verify the accuracy of each transaction at the end of the monthly billing cycle.

steps.action: Attaches supporting documentation for each transaction to the statement, plus a written explanation for any transaction lacking documentation.
steps.source_quote: The documentation should be attached to the statement when it is submitted to the AO.

steps.action: Applies pay-and-confirm. Confirms with the vendor that items are in transit or will be replaced or repaired, pays the invoice in full, and tracks the open transactions in a suspense file.
steps.input: Billed but undelivered, or damaged under-warranty items
steps.source_quote: The CH will confirm with the vendor that the items ordered are in transit

steps.action: Certifies the bank statement and forwards all documentation to the AO/CO.
steps.source_quote: The CH will certify the bank statement and forward all documentation to the AO/CO.

steps.action: Reconciles the CH's statement in CITIBANK and ensures purchases were appropriate and charges accurate. Verifies supporting documentation and confirms receipt, inspection, and acceptance (e.g., initials on receipts).
steps.source_quote: Reconcile the CH's monthly statement in CITIBANK.

steps.action: Notifies the A/OPC or NETC N4 of a suspected unauthorized purchase (noncompliance, fraud, misuse, or abuse).
steps.source_quote: Notify the A/OPC or NETC N4 in the event of any suspected unauthorized purchase

steps.action: Certifies the monthly invoice and forwards it to the appropriate office for payment.
steps.source_quote: Certify the monthly invoice within 10 business days

steps.action: Completes the monthly PAT review and returns all supporting documentation to the CH.
steps.output: Completed PAT review; documentation returned to CH
steps.source_quote: Complete the monthly PAT Review within 15 calendar days of the end of the billing cycle

steps.action: Conducts the monthly program review of transactions, targeting internal controls, training, span of control, and delinquencies. The review is automatically submitted to the next higher level A/OPC.
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC shall conduct a review of transactions using the DON Data Mining System PAT

steps.action: Conducts the semi-annual review aggregating the previous six monthly reviews.
steps.system: DON Data Mining System PAT; Semi-Annual Review Auxiliary Worksheet (Appendix D)
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC shall conduct the semi-annual review

steps.action: Reviews and approves the semi-annual report. Once approved, the report is forwarded to the Hierarchy Level 3 A/OPC for submission to CCPMD.
steps.output: Approved report forwarded to Level 3 A/OPC
steps.source_quote: The report shall be provided to the HA (N4) for review and approval.

steps.action: Contacts the A/OPC to determine whether the dispute procedure or the fraud procedure applies. Only one procedure is initiated.
steps.source_quote: The CH or AO must contact the A/OPC to determine which procedure is appropriate

steps.action: Disputes the transaction through the invoice certification process in CitiDirect, which automatically short-pays the invoice.
steps.source_quote: Transactions must be disputed through the invoice certification process within CitiDirect.

steps.action: Signs the CITIBANK Government Cardholder Dispute Form (Appendix B) and sends it to CITIBANK by fax or mail.
steps.source_quote: submit/fax the CITIBANK Government Cardholder Dispute Form (Appendix B) to CITIBANK at 605-357-2019

steps.action: Tracks the dispute to resolution.
steps.source_quote: Track the dispute to resolution either by calling CITIBANK or reviewing the CITIBANK dispute log within CitiDirect.

steps.action: Notifies the A/OPC immediately of suspected fraudulent activity on the account.
steps.source_quote: The CH must notify the A/OPC immediately of any suspected fraudulent activity on the account.

steps.action: Contacts CITIBANK. The account is closed and a replacement account and card are issued.
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC will contact CITIBANK.

steps.action: Confirms with the CH which transactions are valid and which are fraudulent. Moves valid transactions to the new account.
steps.output: Valid transactions moved to new account
steps.source_quote: The bank will confirm with the CH which transactions are valid and which are fraudulent

steps.action: Completes the Declaration of Unauthorized Use form (Appendix C) for submission to the bank, then follows further A/OPC guidance.
steps.source_quote: the CH will complete a Declaration of Unauthorized Use form (Appendix C) to be submitted to the bank.

steps.action: Short-pays the invoice by the amount of the fraudulent transactions and certifies it using the manual certification process, not the dispute process.
steps.source_quote: certified using the manual certification process, not the dispute process.

decisions.condition: Is the request unusual or questionable?
Is funding available for the requirement?
Is additional documentation (SF 182 or NETC 4235/4) required?
Is the SF 182 training request valued above $25,000?
Does the AO approve the purchase?
Does the purchase exceed the CH's single purchase limit?
Is the merchant's price fair and reasonable?
Is the item accountable property ($5,000+ unit cost, or sensitive, pilferable, or classified)?
Does the statement show an unrecognized or invalid transaction?
Was the CH billed for items not yet received, or for damaged items the contractor will replace or repair under warranty?
Was the material received, or the transaction/credit posted, within the next billing cycle?
Is any purchase suspected to be unauthorized (noncompliance, fraud, misuse, or abuse)?
Does the HA (N4) approve the semi-annual report?
Is the suspect transaction fraudulent rather than a dispute?
Was the dispute resolved in favor of the CH?

branches.label: Yes (offset by vendor or bank credit)
No (charge appears on next invoice and must be certified)

exceptions.trigger: Participant does not complete refresher training within two years
exceptions.handling: Account is suspended until training is completed.

exceptions.trigger: CH is transferred, separated, or retires
exceptions.handling: Appointment ends. The A/OPC ensures, to the maximum extent possible, that the account is inactive at least 30 days before departure, and closes it once all transactions and payments clear. If transactions remain outstanding, the A/OPC reduces the limits to $1.00 and cuts up the card. All GCPC files are turned in to the AO/CO for retention.

exceptions.trigger: Request is unusual or questionable
exceptions.handling: Forwarded for review before any action is taken. The SOP does not state what happens after the review.

exceptions.trigger: Funding is exhausted
exceptions.handling: Requirements are forwarded to the Comptroller for review. The outcome and next step are not stated.

exceptions.trigger: SF 182 training request exceeds $25,000
exceptions.handling: The GCPC may not be used. No alternative path is stated.

exceptions.trigger: AO does not approve the purchase
Merchant's price is not fair and reasonable
Merchant will ship only FOB origin / prepay and add
exceptions.handling: CH should not accept FOB origin unless the merchant states it is the only way they will ship.

exceptions.trigger: Transaction is denied by the CITIBANK authorization system
Card is lost or stolen
exceptions.handling: CH immediately calls CITIBANK (1-800-790-7206). The CH notifies the AO and A/OPC within one business day, and the AO submits a written report to the A/OPC within one business day. CITIBANK mails a replacement card. A card found later is cut in half and given to the AO or A/OPC.

exceptions.trigger: Emergent situation prevents three-way separation of function
exceptions.handling: Minimum two-way separation applies: the person who awarded the order does not perform receipt, inspection, or acceptance.

exceptions.trigger: CH is not available to review the statement for certification
exceptions.handling: CH notifies the AO. The AO reviews the statement and documentation and certifies the account for payment, then meets with the CH on their return to review the statement.

exceptions.trigger: CH has no documentation for a transaction
exceptions.handling: CH attaches an explanation with item description, cost, transaction date, merchant name, price, quantity, and the reason documentation is missing.

exceptions.trigger: Billed material is not received within the next billing cycle
exceptions.handling: CH disputes the item using established dispute procedures.

exceptions.trigger: Warranty transactions or credits do not post on the next billing statement
exceptions.handling: CH or AO notifies the A/OPC to resolve and reconcile the statement.

exceptions.trigger: AO/CO suspects an unauthorized purchase
exceptions.handling: Notify the A/OPC or NETC N4. Supervisors who learn of misuse take appropriate action, including investigation. No further process steps are defined.

exceptions.trigger: Suspect transaction is reported as both a dispute and fraud
exceptions.handling: Prohibited; only one procedure may be initiated. Using both may cause incorrect short-payment and account delinquency.

exceptions.trigger: Dispute is resolved in favor of the merchant
exceptions.handling: A letter is sent to the CH explaining the decision. The charge appears on the next invoice and must be certified for payment.

exceptions.trigger: Local program fails the external PMR review
exceptions.handling: All card accounts are suspended for three days except one CH and one AO account for mission-essential needs. Mandatory stand-down training is held and a Plan of Action and Milestones is prepared.

exceptions.trigger: HA (N4) does not approve the semi-annual report

timing.requirement: Initial training before assuming program responsibility. Refresher training within two years of initial or last refresher training. DoD ethics training annually. COs and D/AOs complete Certifying Officer Legislation training annually.
Requirements are discussed with department heads and program managers, and LOAs issued, before the start of the new fiscal year.
N8 provides funds status updates only 'occasionally or upon request' (no fixed interval).
Merchant must deliver, or have available for pickup, all items no later than 30 days from the order date.
Performed at the end of the monthly billing cycle. The cycle ends on the 19th of each month, or the preceding Friday if the 19th falls on a weekend.
Material, replacement, or credit is expected within the next billing cycle.
CH and AO/CO complete reconciliation within five business days of the statement status changing from INTERIM to NEW.
Certify the monthly invoice within 10 business days of the statement status changing from INTERIM to NEW.
Complete the monthly PAT review within 15 calendar days of the end of the billing cycle.
A/OPC completes the monthly review within 30 calendar days of the end of the billing cycle.
Semi-annual review covers billing cycles 20 March-19 September and 20 September-19 March.
CH has 60 days from the billing statement date to formally dispute transactions.
Notify the A/OPC immediately of suspected fraud. Fraudulent accounts are closed immediately.

Lost or stolen card: call CITIBANK immediately. Notify the AO and A/OPC within one business day, and the AO's written report is due within one business day. CITIBANK mails a replacement within one business day.
On CH departure, the account should be inactive at least 30 days (one billing cycle) before departure and must not remain active past the official departure date.
External PMR desk audit occurs every 18 months. A subsequent 180-day review follows a failed review.
Financial transaction records are retained for 10 years.

risks.description: Section 6.c says 'Requests are emailed to N8.' No request log, status, or queue is defined, so requests can sit in an inbox with no tracking or audit trail.

Section 6.c sends unusual or questionable requests to the Deputy Comptroller, Comptroller, and 'possibly Legal (N00D)'. The SOP does not say who decides when Legal is involved, what the review outcomes are, or what happens next (D1 Yes branch has no return path).
Section 6.e: if funding is exhausted, requirements are forwarded to the Comptroller for review. The outcome and next step are not stated, and the requestor and CH are not told what happens.

Section 6.e: funds status updates come 'occasionally or upon request'. Section 6.a: 'Specific dollar amounts are not assigned.' Yet CHs must ensure funds are committed before buying (7.a(2)). With no fixed reporting interval, purchases could proceed against funds that are already exhausted.
Decision D4 (16.b): the GCPC may not be used for SF 182 training above $25,000. No alternative procurement path or owner is stated.

Two sections describe preparing the same SF 182 and distributing paper copies. Under 6.b/6.d the requestor sends signed copies to N8 and the CH. Under 16.c/16.d the division assigns an LOA, gets CH details by contacting N4, and sends copies to N4 and HRO. The LOA and CH data are re-entered and copies multiply across four parties.
Decision D5: the SOP requires AO approval before purchasing (7.a(3)) but states no next step when the AO does not approve. The requestor may never be told, and the request has no closure.

Section 7.a(3) says 'Obtain AO approval prior to purchasing' but names no form or record for the approval. Section 7.e still expects documentation of required special approvals, so approvals may be undocumented when the AO later reviews.

N4 holds many roles. It serves as AO for supplies (6.a), approves exceptions to the single purchase limit (8), and performs the A/OPC function as GCPC Program Manager at a single phone number (3.b). It also holds the delegated HA responsibilities (3.a) and maintains DPAS (14.b). No backup or alternate is named for any of these roles.
Decision D7 (7.b): the CH may purchase only if the merchant's price is fair and reasonable. No next step is stated when it is not, such as selecting another merchant or returning to the AO.

The CH types each transaction into the NETC 4430/1 log (7.e). The same data then appears on the CITIBANK statement and is reconciled by the CH (S21) and again by the AO/CO in CITIBANK (S25). The same transaction data is handled in multiple places.

Section 9.a: receipt/inspection and acceptance pass among three people by 'legible signature and date' on paper, with no tracking. Section 10.b(5) lets the AO confirm this 'by placing initials in a corner' of receipts, a weak and easily missed check.
Section 14.a: 'AOs and CHs identify whether materials need to be recorded' gives joint ownership and no timing. Accountable, sensitive, or pilferable items could go unrecorded in DPAS.

Under pay-and-confirm (10.a(1)-(2)) the CH pays in full and tracks open items in a paper suspense file. Nothing checks that unreceived items are disputed within the 60-day window (11.a(5)), so payment for undelivered goods could become unrecoverable.

The deadlines overlap. Section 10 says CH and AO/CO complete reconciliation within 5 business days of INTERIM to NEW. Section 10.b(6) allows 10 business days for certification, and 10.b(7) allows 15 calendar days from cycle end for PAT. No deadline is set for the CH-to-AO/CO handoff.

The CH forwards 'all documentation' to the AO/CO (10), and the AO later returns it to the CH (10.b(7)). This paper package moves twice with no tracking, while records must be retained for 10 years (21).

Section 10.b(4): after the AO/CO notifies the A/OPC or N4 of a suspected unauthorized purchase, no further steps are defined. The SOP does not say whether certification is held or who investigates. Section 13.b says only that supervisors 'take appropriate action'.

Sections 3.c and 3.d: 'The same person performs the roles of AO and CO.' The official who approves purchases before buying (7.a(3)) also certifies the same charges for payment, with no independent check before money is released.

Section 22.b: the A/OPC's semi-annual review is approved by the HA (N4). Sections 3.a and 3.b: HA responsibilities are delegated to N4, and the GCPC Program Manager (N4) performs the A/OPC function. The program oversight report is effectively approved by the office that produced it.
Decision D13: no next step is stated if the HA (N4) does not approve the semi-annual report.
Section 11.a(2): the CH disputes the transaction in CitiDirect, then submits the same details again on the Appendix B paper form by fax or mail.
Section 11.a(3): 'Track the dispute to resolution' names no actor and no check frequency (11.a names the 'CH or AO'). Open disputes could go unmonitored.

Section 11.b(1): suspected fraud must be reported to the A/OPC 'immediately', and the A/OPC contacts CITIBANK. The A/OPC function is held by the GCPC Program Manager (N4) (3.b). No backup is named for an urgent report when that person is unavailable.
Section 11.b(3): the CH 'will follow further guidance provided by the A/OPC', with no deadline for submitting the Declaration of Unauthorized Use.

Section 20: on CH departure, the A/OPC makes the account inactive 'to the maximum extent possible' and reduces limits 'as soon as practical'. The SOP does not say how the A/OPC learns of a departure, so an active card could stay open past the CH's departure.

Section 5.b: failure to complete refresher training suspends the account. Certificates go to the A/OPC (5.c(2)), but no one is named to track the two-year and annual due dates or to trigger the suspension.

starter_flows.trigger: When an item is created in the SharePoint 'GCPC Purchase Requests' list (submitted from the Power Apps request form)
actions: Get the requestor's department and the request details: description, category, estimated cost, need date
Check required fields; if missing, email the requestor and set status to 'Returned - incomplete'
If the category is training or material, set the 'Additional documentation required' flag and email the requestor a link to the SF 182 / NETC 4235/4 form
Set status to 'Submitted to N8' and stamp the submission date
Post a notification with the item link to the N8 Teams channel or shared mailbox
Create a 'Request history' entry for the audit trail
starter_flows.approval_step: N8 'Start and wait for an approval' (custom responses): 'Routine - assign LOA', 'Forward for Deputy Comptroller/Comptroller/Legal review', or 'Funding exhausted - forward to Comptroller'; record the response and comments on the request item

starter_flows.trigger: When a SharePoint 'GCPC Purchase Requests' item is modified and status equals 'Screened' (CH has recorded the mandatory-source screening)
actions: Get the CH's single purchase limit and assigned AO from the SharePoint CH roster
Compare the estimated cost to the single purchase limit
Send the AO approval request (N4 for supplies/equipment/printing; N8 for training and centrally managed)
If the cost exceeds the single purchase limit, send a second approval request to N4
If approved, set status to 'Approved to purchase', record the approver and date, and notify the CH

Look up the Receiver/Inspector and Acceptor from the roster, excluding the CH, and assign them on the log item
Notify the Receiver/Inspector of the expected delivery and set a reminder at 30 days from the order date
